subject: Discovery: Private/VPC requirements for MediCore — recap & next steps
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Byrne <alice.byrne@medicorehealth.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-15T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Discovery: Private/VPC requirements for MediCore — recap & next steps

Hi Alice —

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we have a shared starting point and clear next steps. Please flag anything we missed or got wrong.

Top pain points you shared
- Current hosted vendors are showing unpredictable latency and high per-token cost for on-prem workloads.
- Security/compliance requires customer-managed keys and strict network isolation for PHI workloads.
- Procurement timeline: POC + security review to start before Q3 procurement window.

Current stack & constraints
- Primary apps run in your private VPC in AWS (us-east-1) behind strict egress controls.
- Centralized KMS managed by your security team (you called out HSM-backed keys).
- Network: no direct public IPs on compute nodes; all outbound must go through approved NAT or proxy.
- Ops: internal network team requires a diagram and specific port/IP rules before any deployment.

Success criteria you described
- Demo POC (on Private deployment) that can serve 95th pct latency under 250ms for 512-token sequences.
- Evidence of KMS integration + audit logs accessible by your security team.
- Clear mutual action plan covering timeline, procurement, and support SLAs.

Must-have technical items (we heard)
1) Private control plane with encrypted control channel or VPC peering.
2) Bring-your-own-KMS (BYOK) with HSM option.
3) Ability to deploy in an air-gapped or restricted network mode if required.
4) Audit logs and token-level access controls retained per your retention policy.
5) Network diagram + firewall rule template to satisfy network review.

Questions / asks from Redwood to unblock next steps
- Can you share a high-level network diagram showing the VPC, subnets, and NAT/proxy points? (attachment preferred)
- Confirm whether egress to a Redwood control plane is allowed from a limited set of IPs, or whether you require an entirely private control plane.
- Who is the primary network owner and CISO we should schedule a short technical sync with?

Attachments: redwood-onprem-questions.pdf (short questionnaire we use to accelerate technical review)

Proposed next steps
- You to send network diagram + the Security-Reqs spreadsheet (you mentioned Tom would provide).
- Redwood to prepare an options matrix for VPC connectivity and BYOK flow by next Wednesday.
- Schedule tech sync (1 hour) with your network/CISO and our infra lead (Dev).

Proposed times for tech sync (PST):
- Wed 2026-06-17 10:00–11:00 or Thu 2026-06-18 13:00–14:00

Thanks — happy to adjust.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
T: +1 (415) 555-0142
E: tessa.morgan@redwood.ai

Tessa — thank you for the clear write-up. This looks right to me and helpful to get everyone aligned. A few clarifications and I attached the network diagram + our current security requirements spreadsheet.

Clarifications
- Timeline: internal goal is to have vendor security reviews completed by the end of July so we can start a limited POC in August.
- KMS: we operate a centralized AWS KMS with an HSM-backed key policy; we can provide a dedicated key for this project.
- Egress: we cannot allow arbitrary outbound traffic. We prefer either VPC peering with a private control plane or tightly controlled outbound to an approved IP range.

Attached

Tom (cc'd) is our CISO and will be looped into the tech sync — he can speak to audit and retention policies.

We'll look at the redwood-onprem-questions and aim to get back with answers by EOD Thursday. If possible, can you have a draft of the VPC connectivity options ahead of the tech sync? That will help the network team evaluate quickly.

Thanks,
Alice Byrne

Subject: Re: Discovery: Private/VPC requirements for MediCore — recap & next steps

Alice — thanks for sending the diagram and the security spreadsheet. Quick technical follow-ups from my side so we can scope the POC accurately: 

1) Control plane connectivity
- We can support two patterns: (A) Private control plane reachable via VPC peering (no public egress from compute), or (B) a public control plane with tightly restricted egress to a known set of Redwood IPs and mTLS. Option A is preferred for your "no outbound" constraint but requires peering setup.

2) KMS / BYOK
- Redwood supports a BYOK flow with AWS KMS and can integrate with HSM-backed keys. We'll need an IAM role and a limited cross-account policy for the key; we can provide a template.

3) Network specifics we need from you to prepare the firewall template:
- CIDR ranges of subnets that will host inference nodes
- Any required proxy/NAT IPs for egress (if Option B)
- List of ports allowed by the network team (we typically need 443 and a small control port range; we'll provide exact ports)

4) Air-gap / on-prem option
- For fully air-gapped deployments we can provide an appliance + offline installer process. That path increases lead time and requires on-site support during install. If you think this is likely, please flag early.

Attached: VPC-connect-options.md (outlines the peering vs egress patterns with pros/cons).

If helpful, Dev and I can put together a short diagram showing the peering + KMS key flow for your network team to review.

Next actions I can take immediately:
- Draft the cross-account KMS policy and share by Tue EOD.
- Prepare a one-page firewall rule template once you provide CIDRs.
- Build a short tech-deck for the CISO call showing latency expectations and audit log flows.

I'll coordinate with Tessa on scheduling.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Principal Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference
dev.patel@redwood.ai
